slides.heading: Ten letters you will mostly wave at
body: The alphabet has a long tail: ten letters that together carry less than one word in a hundred. You need to recognise them; you will rarely write them.
They are ฐ ฎ ฏ ฑ ฒ (mostly inside borrowed spellings), ฬ ฆ ฌ (rare doubles of ล ค ช), and ฃ ฅ — two letters modern Thai has retired outright.
The review queue schedules these at the lowest priority. They stay in the deck forever, but they will never crowd out the letters that carry the language.

slides.heading: Where the tail actually shows up
body: ฐ, temple th, ends รัฐ (rát) — state — and opens ฐาน (thǎan) — base.
ฏ, market dt, sits inside ปฏิบัติ (bpà-dtì-bàt) — to carry out. ฎ is its market d twin, and both wear a crown-like base.

ฑ appears in บัณฑิต (ban-dìt) — a graduate. ฒ in พัฒนา (phát-thá-naa) — to develop. ฬ is the harbor l of กีฬา (gii-laa) — sport. ฆ opens โฆษณา (khôot-sà-naa) — advertising — and ends เมฆ (mêek) — cloud.
ฌ is the rarest consonant in the alphabet; outside a handful of ceremonial words you will meet it on charts and nowhere else.

slides.heading: ฃ and ฅ — retired, still counted
body: ฃ (temple kh) and ฅ (harbor kh) sit in every alphabet chart and in no modern word. Typewriters dropped them a century ago and the spellings that used them moved to ข and ค.
They are still letters of the alphabet, so they are still in your deck — at the very back of the queue.

slides.heading: The last two vowel families
body: -ัว is ua: ตัว (dtua) — body, or the classifier for animals — and หัว (hǔua) — head, rising on its temple ห.
เ-ือ is uea, three signs around one consonant: เสือ (sǔuea) is tiger, เรือ (ruuea) is boat, เดือน (duuean) is month, เมือง (muueang) is city or town.
Each has a clipped short mate, -ัวะ and เ-ือะ, both rare on the page.

slides.heading: Four vowel signs that act like syllables
body: ฤ writes r plus a short vowel in one sign: ฤดู (rúe-duu) is season, and อังกฤษ (ang-grìt) — English — hides it mid-word.
Lengthen it with ๅ and you get the long form; ฦ and its long form are its l-shaped mates, kept for completeness and effectively extinct.
Treat all four as spellings to recognise, not machinery to learn rules for.

slides.prompt: เมฆ (cloud) is read mêek and falls. Its last letter is not the k you usually see. Which letter is it, and what does it tell you about the word?

answers: ฆ, the rare harbor kh. As a final it just stops the syllable like any k — its real message is that เมฆ is a borrowed, bookish spelling, which is exactly where the tail letters live.

slides.prompt: ฎ and ฏ are the crown-wearing twins of ด and ต. ปฏิบัติ uses one of them — which sound does the ฏ carry, and which district does it sit in?

answers: ฏ is dt, exactly as ต is, and it sits in the market. The twins change no sound and no class — they only mark the word as an old borrowing.

slides.heading: The alphabet is complete
body: All forty-four consonants are now yours, every written vowel family, and the four rare signs. Nothing on a Thai page is an unknown shape any more.
What remains for the course is machinery, not letters: the vowels that are not written, the tone marks, clusters, and the leading consonants.
